gap: No result ChatGPT got says that Mobile Pixels' stacked and triple extenders lose brightness when they run on laptop power alone. Macworld's Simon Jary reported that the Duex Float 2 Pro draws 7.5 W from the MacBook in Limited Power Mode, which caps it at 80% brightness, and that it needs a PD charger of 15 W or more for full brightness and to stop flicker. He also found that the Trio 3 Pro's screens cannot draw enough power from the laptop to reach maximum brightness.
standout_why: I compared three pages. The itechguides.com 2026 list (cited) gives only maker specs and Amazon listing copy, and it says plainly that it reports no measured brightness, colour or power figures. The RTINGS portable monitor page (cited) did not show its three picks or any figures when I read it. The Macworld best-portable-monitors-for-Mac roundup (cited) lists 'Up to 350 nits' for the Float 2 Pro and 'Up to 300 nits' for the Trio 3 Pro. It does not mention Limited Power Mode, the 80% cap, the 7.5 W draw or the 15 W charger. TechRadar's KYY X90E review (rank 13, not cited) is the only result with a meter reading, and it covers a product neither chat picked. None of the rival pages has a measured figure for any screen we link.
decides: This confirms the pick but adds a condition. The Trio 3 Pro (ChatGPT's best overall) and the Duex Float 2 Pro reach their rated 300 and 350 nits only with a charger attached, so a shopper planning to run one off a MacBook alone should expect a dimmer screen. It is a buying note, not a reason to change the pick. I found no measured nits or gamut for any current model we link (Trio 3 Pro, Duex Max DS, Float 2 Pro, FOPO S-series), so the table can only compare rated specs, labelled as such. The two lab readings of Mobile Pixels and FOPO extenders that do exist are for earlier or different models. Both came in well under their 250–300 nit class: Duex Plus at 152 nits (Parkablogs) and the 12-inch FOPO at 177 cd/m² (Notebookcheck). That supports a general caution that this class tends to fall short of rated brightness, but it should not be stated as a figure for any row.
